title: Progressive tenant sharding and adaptive backpressure for Dedicated/Private
creator: Emily Rivera
description: Implement a progressive tenant sharding strategy combined with adaptive backpressure and circuit-breaker tiers to protect Dedicated and Private control planes during upgrades, region failovers, and noisy-tenant incidents. The goal is to preserve SLOs for high-priority tenants while providing graceful degradation for best-effort workloads and minimizing cross-tenant blast radius. This ticket scopes: shard allocation policy, run-time admission controls, dynamic circuit-breaker thresholds, region-affinity failover policy, and an upgrade-safe tenant drain workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Sharding policy implemented: tenants are placed into primary and secondary shards with weight metadata and affinity tags
Admission controller enforces per-shard qps and concurrent request limits and can downgrade non-critical requests to best-effort queues
Circuit-breaker tiers implemented (soft-warning, reject, isolate) with configurable percentiles (p50/p95/p99) tied to latency and CPU/KV cache contention metrics
Automated failover policy moves only affected shards to secondary region with controlled ramp (10% shard batch every 30s) to avoid thundering herd
Upgrade workflow: staged drain + emergency abort that preserves pinned tenants and triggers fallback models; verified in canary cluster without SLO regression
End-to-end tests that simulate noisy-tenant spike, region loss, and rolling upgrade show no more than 3% SLO degradation for P1/P0 tenants and isolation for affected lower-tier tenants
Docs and runbook published with dashboard links and escalation steps
work_notes: 2025-11-05 - Emily Rivera: Initial write-up and triage. Framed problem after last incident where a single onboarding tenant caused KV cache thrash during Dedicated cluster upgrade. Proposed progressive sharding instead of all-or-nothing tenant throttles.

2025-11-07 - Design review with Platform (Dana Lee): Agreed on three shard tiers (critical, standard, best-effort). Dana asked for explicit spec on migration semantics when moving shards between regions; flagged data-plane affinity for sessions.

2025-11-09 - Engineering sync: Decided to implement admission controller as extension to existing gateway with feature flag. Trade-offs: gateway-level checks add tail latency (~2-3ms) vs faster isolation when implemented deeper. We prefer quicker mitigation and simpler rollout.

2025-11-10 - Spike results: microbenchmarks show admission checks add median +2ms and p99 +8ms under load; acceptable for P0 customers if we gate via feature flag and use fast-path for pinned tenants.
2025-11-12 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4823 - implements shard metadata and admission binding. (PR links require review)

2025-11-13 - Ops feedback (Jamal Torres): Add explicit circuit-breaker metric exports: breaker_state, breaker_rejections, breaker_latency_window. Ops wants these exported to Datadog and alertable at >1% rejection sustained for 5m.

2025-11-14 - Risk discussion: Ravi argued for a soft-warning tier before reject to allow graceful client degradation; Emily recommended best-effort downgrade (reduce temperature, sampling, or model size) for noncritical tenants. We will implement both: soft-warning telemetry + fallback to reduced-cost execution path.
2025-11-15 - Security note: Private deployments require audit logging of shard moves and admission rejections. Security review requested (ticket created).

2025-11-16 - Integration tests: Started canary run in dedicated-canary-a with 20 tenants simulated; observed expected behavior: best-effort queue saw 70% request drop during synthetic noisy-tenant spike, critical tenants maintained latency SLOs.
2025-11-17 - PM review (Lara Kim): Approved approach, requested dashboard widget showing tenant shard membership and real-time breaker states. Added to follow-up UI ticket.
2025-11-18 - Next steps: finish circuit-breaker exporter, complete PR review, add runbook play for emergency shard quiesce, schedule staged canary across two regions next week
runbook_excerpt: When breaker enters 'isolate' for a shard: 1) Pause noncritical shard migrations, 2) Scale up shard compute by +15% for 5m if available, 3) If sustained >3m, move shard to secondary region using progressive ramp.

During rolling upgrade: 1) Mark critical/pinned tenants with 'no-drain' tag, 2) Drain nodes in batches of 5% tenants at a time, monitor p95 latency for critical tenants, 3) Abort upgrade if p95 for critical tenants increases >20% for two consecutive intervals
tests: Load test harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/load-tests/pull/129 - added noisy-tenant spike scenarios and region failover simulation
Chaos test: cluster-sim regression run scheduled for 2025-11-22 (simulate region-blackout and upgrade concurrently)
review_feedback: Platform review (Dana Lee): Please add explicit session affinity spec for long-running chat sessions and note implications for KV cache warmup
Ops review (Jamal Torres): Export breaker metrics and add synthetic transaction that exercises fallback path every 10m so we can validate end-to-end
PM review (Lara Kim): Ensure UI shows tenant priority and active shard so customers can reason about behavior during incidents
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Shard migration could cause temporary KV cache cold-start and latency spikes. Mitigation: warm-up threads + prefetch top-K cache entries for tenants being moved.
Risk: Admission checks add extra latency. Mitigation: fast-path for pinned tenants and sampling-based checks for low-risk flows.
Risk: Incorrect shard placement might violate data residency. Mitigation: enforce hard constraints on region tags in placement engine and fail allocation if constraints unsatisfiable
